title: YLEH: A look ahead to Indiana's 4th Congressional District Republican Primary - NewsBreak
text:
By Hannah Adamson No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago
INDIANAPOLIS — In the Republican primary for Indiana’s 4 th Congressional District seat, incumbent Congressman Jim Baird and two challengers, State Rep. Craig Haggard (R-Mooresville) and John Piper are hoping to win over voters in West Central Indiana.
“I think we have to stand up for our country, and I intend to do that as long as I can,” Rep. Baird said.
“I can guarantee I’ll continue to fight, and I think that’s something I learned not only from my family, but the Marine Corps: that I will fight,” State Rep. Haggard said. “You get knocked down, you get back up, and I’ll keep fighting for the people.”
With affordability top of mind for most voters, both Haggard and Baird have said that strengthening energy independence is key.
“You know, I think the biggest key to the cost of living that kind of affects everything is energy costs,” Haggard said. “I think we need to get back to real energy, not subsidized energy that we can’t rely on.”
”I really do think the fact that…we went from energy independence to energy dependence and then the dependence was on our adversaries is unbelievable to me,” Baird said.
As the War in Iran rages, Baird has said he’s confident in President Trump’s ability to negotiate his way out of the conflict sooner rather than later.
“I think it’s really time to put the pressure on, and I think the president and his team is doing just that,” Baird said.
Haggard said he could support more guardrails on the war powers within the executive branch.
“I think people forget that Congress is a check on the executive branch,” Haggard said. “I fought in wars, I’ve lost friends, and I don’t take that lightly, so I think anywhere we go, the Congress needs to weigh in.”
The race comes as Gov. Braun reaffirmed support to potentially legalize medical marijuana in the Hoosier State. Last week, the Trump Administration reclassified state-licensed medical cannabis as a less dangerous drug.
“I’m torn on one side for letting people that, if they have benefit from a medical standpoint, I feel for that kind of situation,” Baird said. “But on the other hand…you have to weigh both sides and we have to look for what we think is valid.”
“I look at that, at least on the medical side, from the perspective of a military guy who’s been involved in studies to help veterans with PTSD and traumatic brain injury and what drugs you can use, and I know there’s some benefits for sure with this,” Haggard said.
The race has revealed somewhat of an internal rift within the MAGA coalition of the Republican Party, with President Trump endorsing Baird and Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita endorsing Haggard.
“I think I’ve shown that I’ll fight and I’ll work,” Haggard said. “I’ll be within the district. I’m available. I’ve given my number out to probably a few thousand people, and I’ve done that when I was a state [representative], and I want to remain accountable to the people, and I think they need that.”
“We’re endorsed by the president,” Baird said. “We’re endorsed by [the] NRA. We’re endorsed by Right to Life, and so we are very comfortable with the people that are supporting us and telling us to move forward.”
FOX 59/CBS4 reached out to candidate John Piper for comment and has yet to hear back.
